observation.description: All three n38 versions contain exactly two T tokens; n40 contains no math tokens.

observation.model: u=A*cos(omega*t-k*x); a=-omega^2*u; at u=0 the speed can be maximal, while at |u|=A speed is zero.
observation.limitation: Checks the stated single outgoing small-amplitude oscillatory model, not all possible string disturbances.

observation.model: For cos(omega*t-k*x), adjacent phase delay k*dx is positive and the local frequency is omega. Displacement perpendicular/parallel to the chain distinguishes transverse/longitudinal motion.
observation.limitation: Assumes a supported outgoing propagation mode after the initial transient and before reflected waves return; discrete-chain dispersion is not being simulated.

observation.model: Conserved outgoing power gives I=P/(4*pi*r^2); at fixed impedance/frequency, amplitude-squared tracks intensity. A fixed-area ideal plane-wave tube has constant intensity without loss.
observation.syntheticTestOnly: Doubling radius reduces spherical intensity to one quarter but leaves the fixed-area plane-wave intensity unchanged.
observation.limitation: No values or inverse-radius formula were added to the cards; this is not a general proof for heterogeneous media, interference or near fields.

observation.model: At fixed time, planes normal to k have constant k dot x; tangential displacement leaves phase unchanged. Equal amplitude alone does not impose equal phase. Spherical rays are radial normals.
observation.limitation: Alignment of ray/phase normal with energy transport is restricted to the stated uniform isotropic ray model.

observation.model: Small pure transverse shear has zero strain trace. In the ordinary elastic continuum model, cS^2=G/rho and cP^2=(K+4G/3)/rho; G=0 eliminates bulk elastic shear propagation while K>0 allows longitudinal waves.
observation.limitation: No claim about arbitrary high-frequency viscoelastic or nonmechanical waves; gravity and surface tension can restore liquid-surface motion without bulk shear stiffness.

observation.model: For positive K,G,rho, cP^2-cS^2=(K+G/3)/rho>0. For common-path constant-speed waves, dt=d*(1/cS-1/cP), so a positive S-P delay can be inverted for distance, not unique direction.
observation.limitation: Synthetic constant-speed inversion is illustrative only. Real travel-time curves require source depth and a path/velocity model.

meaning: Fail-capable structural and conditional-model consistency observations supporting, not replacing, the independent sentence-by-sentence SCI judgment
